detailed_findings.finding: Core argument is sound: w_i + w_j lies in S in the relevant residue class, so minimality of the corresponding w_r yields the claimed inequalities after substitution.
The conclusion 'hence k_r >= 1' after ruling out k_r = 0 implicitly uses that w_r ∈ N0 and 1 ≤ r < m, which excludes k_r < 0.

reason: The proof correctly establishes existence of the least representative in each nonzero residue class using cofiniteness of the complement, then derives each Kunz inequality from closure under addition and minimality of the corresponding w_r. The case split matches the lemma statement exactly, with no substantive semantic drift. The only minor implicit step is excluding negative k_r when concluding positivity, but this follows immediately from w_r ∈ N0 and 1 ≤ r ≤ m-1.
